source.title: Prestopping: How Does Early Stopping Help Generalization against Label Noise?
source.authors: Hwanjun Song; Minseok Kim; Dongmin Park; Jae-Gil Lee

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper measures how memorization of true-labeled and false-labeled samples changes over training under label noise, bearing conceptually on V6. Its own results do not test random-label fitting or the other listed versions.
record.gate_note: The paper cites Zhang et al. (2017) for fitting arbitrary label noise and Arpit et al. (2017) for learning easy patterns first; those cited findings are not this paper's results. Test-error comparisons and safe-set precision/recall results concern Prestopping's noisy-label method and do not measure the behaviors named in V1–V5 or V6.
record.test_reason: Standard-training memorization curves distinguish learning of correct and incorrect labels over time, directly bearing on V6. Prestopping's performance comparisons do not themselves test the claim versions.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the motivating observations: incorrect labels are memorized earlier under pair noise, and noise memorization increases sharply late in training. The paper's main conclusion is that combining early stopping with continued training on a dynamically maintained safe set improves robustness across synthetic and real-world label noise; either Prestopping or Prestopping+ generally achieves the lowest test error among the compared methods.
record.recipe_differences: The study examines temporal memorization under noisy-label training and proposes a two-phase early-stopping method; it does not reproduce the original random-label-fitting experiment.
record.method_sensitivity: Noise type changes the reported memorization pattern: false-labeled samples are memorized faster under pair noise than symmetric noise.
record.peer_reviewed: Presented at the ICML 2020 Workshop on Uncertainty and Robustness in Deep Learning
record.problems: The relevant temporal memorization result is presented in a figure without exact values or stated uncertainty. The reported condition is CIFAR-100 with 40% pair noise, so it does not directly compare true labels with completely random labels.
record.rows_left_out: No other result met the row criteria for the listed versions. Test-error comparisons for Prestopping, Prestopping+, and comparator methods do not measure the behaviors those versions name.

untested.parts: Completely random labeling, near-zero training error, chance test performance, and unchanged architecture and hyperparameters in that setting.
Relative time to fit true versus random labels and convergence slowdown across corruption fractions.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Perfect training fit across corruption fractions and steady test-error degradation through complete randomization; experiments cover only 0–40% corruption and emphasize best test error.
Whether explicit regularization prevents random-label fitting and whether removing it preserves generalization on true labels.
Learning on completely randomized datasets and direct identification of shared patterns; the study measures prediction agreement with correct and incorrect labels.

missing.what: Correct-label memorization recall and memorization precision over standard training for both noise types, including their overlapping learning periods and the late precision decline.

The authors' finding that incorrect labels are memorized earlier under pair noise than symmetric noise, and their explicit qualification that all correct labels are not learned before any incorrect labels. No exact onset values are supplied.
missing.locator: Introduction, first memorization finding; Section 3.1, Noise-Rate Heuristic; Appendix B.2.2

record.verdict_notes: This study is not an original source for V6. The supplied figure text supports qualitative temporal findings but does not provide exact curve values or uncertainty for R1. Imperfect clean/noisy separation qualifies a strict sequential interpretation of V6 without reversing its overall tendency.

versions.untested_parts: The paper does not train on completely random labels or report training error and test error at chance for that setting.
No comparison of training time or convergence speed for random versus true labels, or across corruption fractions.
No shuffled-pixel, permuted-pixel, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
The paper varies label-noise rates and reports test errors, but does not report perfect training fit across those rates or steadily rising test error toward chance.
It does not test whether regularization or augmentation prevents random-label fitting, or whether removing them harms true-label generalization.

The paper studies memorization of noisy labels over training, including pair and symmetric noise, but does not compare real labels with completely random labels or report a direct comparison of their learning curves.

rows.subject: DenseNet (L=40, k=12)
rows.operation_detail: Tracked memorization ratios for true-labeled and false-labeled samples during standard training on noisy labels.
rows.measure: Memorization ratio over epochs for true-labeled and false-labeled samples.
rows.value: The false-labeled-sample memorization ratio increases rapidly at a late stage of training, after the error-prone period begins.
rows.note: The figure shows the two memorization-ratio curves; the text describes the late increase in false-labeled-sample memorization. No exact curve values are stated.
rows.check: The condition and qualitative result are correct. Specify that memorization means agreement with the given label by the most frequent prediction over recent epochs (Definition 2.1), rather than instantaneous training accuracy. Figure 2(a) depicts pair noise only; the comparison with symmetric noise requires the accompanying text and Figure 3(a).
